name: Phishing: Example Sub-Technique
description: Simulate a spear-phishing email with a malicious attachment to test email gateway and endpoint detection.
tools: GoPhish; custom Python script; Cobalt Strike Phishing module
steps:
1. Create a test phishing email with a benign macro-enabled .docx file.
2. Send to a consented test mailbox.
3. Open the attachment and enable macros.
4. Observe process creation and network callbacks.
5. Verify detection via email gateway alert and EDR macro execution alert.
expectedDetection: Email gateway: attachment blocked or quarantined. EDR: macro execution spawning child process (winword.exe -> cmd.exe or powershell.exe). Alert: office macro spawning shell process.
logSource: Email gateway log; Sysmon EID 1 (child process of winword.exe); Windows Security EID 4688; EDR macro alert
notes: Test only — do not use production mailboxes.

name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Example
description: Execute a benign payload via PowerShell to test script-block logging and AMSI detection.
steps:
1. Open PowerShell as a standard user.
2. Run Invoke-Expression with a benign Base64-encoded payload.
3. Observe ScriptBlock logging in Windows PowerShell event log.
4. Attempt AMSI bypass technique (safe PoC only).
5. Verify detection: EID 4104 script block logged; AMSI alert triggered.
expectedDetection: EID 4104: script block logging captures encoded/decoded payload. AMSI: detection of obfuscated or known-bad string pattern. Alert: PowerShell encoded command execution by non-admin user.
logSource: Windows PowerShell EID 4104 (script block log); Sysmon EID 1 (powershell.exe -enc); AMSI provider log
